title: A regular affine ideal generator gives an exact frame of its ideal module

source: Derived local frame formulation of The Stacks Project, Lemma 31.14.2, tag 01WS, proof of (2) => (1), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WS , together with regularity on all opens as in Section 31.15, Lemma 31.15.7, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4S . The formal statement uses the registered kernel realization of the ideal module and records the exact image of its frame. This is the local regular-generator argument used in the nodal Cartier-center step for the Philippon alteration frontier; it does not assert the full alteration theorem.

author: @tomasz
source: Derived integral finite-chart form of the denominator-clearing and twisting argument in the Stacks Project, Lemma 28.18.2 (tag 01PW), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PW , and the proof of Lemma 29.38.7(1), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VG . The projective-coordinate construction uses the public Proved native presentation theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/e1f5bbdc-0754-5d5b-904d-1c5a989b084c . The Philippon alteration development applies this criterion to the same actual glued nodal Cartier modification over a projective base; the full alteration theorem is a separate remaining step.

author: @WillR
source: Elementary finite-set induction. Adjoin weight z: the remainder becomes z times the previous remainder plus (1-z) times the previous nonnegative sum of deficits. The first-order sum of deficits is bounded by the existing number of factors. Induction yields the second factorial count.
